questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is any closed four-sided figure.
questions.misconception: Three sides make a triangle and five make a pentagon — 'quad' means four, so exactly four sides.

questions.prompt: The four angles of any quadrilateral add up to...
questions.explanation: Split a quadrilateral along a diagonal and you get two triangles, each 180° — total 360°.
questions.misconception: A triangle sums to 180° and a single corner is 90° — the four-sided total is always 360°.

questions.prompt: Which has four equal sides AND four right angles?
questions.explanation: A square is the member with both equal sides and right angles.
questions.misconception: A rhombus has equal sides but can lean; a trapezoid only needs one pair of parallels — the square is the strict full package.

questions.prompt: When you push a square frame sideways, it becomes...
questions.explanation: Pushing a square flexes it into a leaning rhombus — four equal sides, tilted corners.
questions.misconception: Flexing changes the angles, not the side count or type — the four equal sides remain, becoming a rhombus.

questions.prompt: Why does adding a diagonal brace stiffen a rectangular frame?
options: It splits the frame into two rigid triangles
questions.explanation: The diagonal divides the quadrilateral into two triangles, and triangles cannot flex.
questions.misconception: Stiffening is about geometry, not weight or length — the diagonal's triangles lock every angle in place.
